top_story: Six months into the nominal Gaza ceasefire, persistent Israeli strikes and repeated truce violations have turned a formal pause into a condition of continuing mass death, with more than 72,000 killed, 172,000 injured, and roughly 10,000 people still missing beneath collapsed neighborhoods. In Al Bureij, one father’s years-long search for the remains of four children killed in an airstrike captures how the war’s toll now extends beyond survival to the denial of burial, closure, and any credible return to civilian life. This entrenched destruction sharpens a wider regional reading that the US-backed Israeli campaign on Iran and across the Gulf has not restored order or deterrence, but instead exposed the coercive limits of American power. The immediate intelligence picture is of a regional security architecture that continues to generate extreme human loss while failing to produce political stability.
